gloss: to keep falling (rain, snow); to continue to fall

definitions.gloss: to keep falling; to continue to fall; to rain/snow continuously
definitions.explanation: Used for precipitation (rain, snow, etc.) that continues without stopping. A compound verb formed from 降る (to fall) + 続く (to continue).

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{三日間|みっかかん}{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}いた。
examples.english: It rained continuously for three days.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}が{朝|あさ}から{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: It has been snowing since morning.

examples.japanese: {梅雨|つゆ}の{時期|じき}は{雨|あめ}が{何日|なんにち}も{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}くので、{洗濯物|せんたくもの}が{乾|かわ}かない。
examples.english: During the rainy season, it rains for days on end, so the laundry won't dry.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {降|ふ}る (to fall — precipitation) + {続|つづ}く (to continue). Used exclusively for precipitation — rain, snow, hail, etc. — falling without interruption.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}く: rain continues to fall
- {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}く: snow continues to fall
- {何日|なんにち}も{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}く: to keep falling for days

COMMON PATTERNS:
Conjugates as a godan verb (く row): {降|ふ}り{続|つづ}かない、{降|ふ}り{続|つづ}いて、etc. The transitive counterpart {降|ふ}り{続|つづ}ける (to keep letting fall) is not normally used, as precipitation is not a volitional action.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {降|ふ}り{止|や}まない: to not stop falling — emphasizes the lack of cessation
- {降|ふ}り{注|そそ}ぐ: to pour down — emphasizes intensity rather than duration
